questions: Did slalom line_loss_events fall from 1.85 back toward 1.0 or below, and did slalom progress rise above 0.17?
Did s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1.0, and did any s-bend max_error drop below the 0.06 m floor?
Did steering_oscillation stay under about 0.35 on the s-bend and oval with the larger footprint? If it rose, did the blurrier edge signal cause the jitter?
Does the oval still finish 20 of 20 with max_error near 0.025?
If the s-bend is unchanged, is the remaining limit controller gain or turn authority, so the next step should be a controller change rather than geometry?

intent: Test whether a larger 16 mm sensor footprint keeps the line in view through the s-bend and slalom. Iteration 3 showed the s-bend still losing the line about once per run at the max_error floor, and slalom line losses rising to 1.85 with wheel_track 0.09. The only change from iteration 3 is sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016, with x positions, y 0.07, wheel_track 0.09, wheel radius, body and mass unchanged. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events back near 1.0 or below, s-bend line_loss_events below 1.0, and s-bend max_error below 0.06 on some seeds, with the oval still finishing 20 of 20.
learning: Iteration 3 showed that wheel_track 0.09 with y 0.07 lifted the score to 448.7 and kept the oval at 20 of 20, but it did not clear the s-bend floor and it worsened slalom line losses to 1.85. Iteration 4 isolates the sensor footprint by changing only sensor_size to 0.016. If slalom losses recover but the s-bend still sits at the floor, the geometry is close to its limit and further gains should come from the controller.
rationale: Iteration 3 (score 448.7, up from 433) narrowed wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m with sensors at y 0.07. The oval still finished 20 of 20 with max_error 0.025 and oscillation 0.21, so the narrower track did not add lag or jitter there. The s-bend improved slightly: 2 of 20 finishes, progress 0.68 (from 0.64), and line_loss_events 1.0 (from 1.05). Oscillation was 0.32, under the 0.35 threshold, so the track change is not too aggressive. However, max_error still sits at the 0.06 m off-track floor (0.0607) and the s-bend is still losing the line about once per run. The slalom got worse: line losses rose from 1.0 to 1.85 per run and progress was 0.17, with no finishes. The Integrator's rules give two triggers. The s-bend rule says that if line losses stay at 1.0 with max_error at the floor and low oscillation, test sensor_size 0.016 with the same x positions and y 0.07. The slalom rule says that if slalom losses rise again, the 12 mm footprint is too narrow and the 16 mm footprint should be tested. Both triggers apply. I therefore change only sensor_size, from 0.012 to 0.016 m. I keep wheel_track at 0.09 m, because the s-bend rule for changing track was not met and changing two things at once would hide the cause. The 16 mm footprints at 15 mm pitch still leave the outer sensors blank on a centred line, so the antisymmetric weights remain valid. Expected result: slalom line losses fall back toward 1.0 or below, s-bend line losses fall below 1.0, and s-bend max_error drops below the 0.06 floor on some seeds. Risk: the larger footprint blurs the edge signal, so the s-bend may not improve and the oval may show more oscillation. The next race must report line losses, max_error and oscillation for each track to test this.
